title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Page 34 of the 1986 manuscript is a terminological digression ('Digression 4') inside Grothendieck's combinatorial, stratified approach to topology.

The setting, from the surrounding pages:
- M is a structured poset whose elements are 'strata', called 'multistrates' when viewed as sets of incident sub-strata.
- Figures F are built from these elements. They are subsets or configurations of M closed under incidence: finite, locally finite or compact figures.
- An 'atelier attenant' is a class of admissible figures attached to M.
- The previous page introduced the 'compactological' setting: the tuple (M, ⊴, 𝓛, |·|, M_c), where M_c ⊂ M is the sub-object of compact strata.

The point made on this page is that foundational work increasingly focuses on M itself rather than on individual figures F. Grothendieck therefore proposes a change of names:
- The word 'atelier' (workshop) should now designate M, which 'works with' its strata or multistrates to build figures.
- The set of figures so built is a 'magasin' (store) attached to the atelier, rather than the other way round.
- Several magasins can be attached to the same atelier, e.g. finite figures, locally finite figures, or all M-figures, as on p.33.
- In the compactological case, M_c (the compact (multi)strata) could be called the 'cœur' (core) of the atelier.

In modern terms, M plays the role of a face or incidence poset of a stratified space. The magasins are families of admissible subcomplexes (order ideals with a finiteness condition). M_c is the sub-poset of compact cells.

The page contains no theorem or construction. It is purely naming and reorganisation, serving the effort to make the combinatorial category of 'stratified figures' the primary object of study. This continues the 'tame topology' programme of Esquisse d'un programme.
errors: No mathematical errors; the page is terminological. The phrase 'peut-être' is written 'peut-être' where 'peut être' is meant (minor orthographic slip).

ideas.what: Shift of emphasis from figures F to the ambient structure M of strata. M is renamed 'atelier', and the set of figures constructed from its strata is renamed 'magasin attenant'; several magasins (finite, locally finite, all figures) can be attached to one atelier.
ideas.modern_name: Face/incidence poset of a stratified or regular CW structure, together with chosen classes of subcomplexes (finite, locally finite) – cf. Alexandrov topologies on posets, cellular stratified spaces, exit-path / poset-stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Alexandrov (posets as spaces, 1937); regular CW / face posets (Björner and others, 1980s); stratified spaces in the tame-topology sense (Grothendieck's Esquisse 1984, later o-minimal geometry by van den Dries and others)
ideas.where_published: Only the general 'tame topology' programme appears in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the atelier/magasin terminology is unpublished as far as I know

ideas.what: 'Cœur' of an atelier: the sub-poset M_c of compact (multi)strata in the compactological setting.
ideas.modern_name: Sub-poset of compact (closure-finite) cells / compactly supported part

deep.surprise_reason: Purely terminological reshuffling (atelier→M, magasin→set of figures, cœur→M_c) within an already-known unpublished project. It has some archival interest for the history of Grothendieck's combinatorial topology, but no new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: Header line reads roughly 'Terminologie : atelier, magasin, strate (multistrates.)', with 'multistrates' added above the line.
'magasin compactologique' is likely correct, though the word is hard to read; it could be 'compactologiste'.
Line 7 of the body: 'Cet atelier travaille avec les objets qui figurent dans M, les {+strates ou+} multistrates' is confirmed.
